name: MemT-1.0 (Nano and Flash)

lineage.how_derived: native memory block added next to attention (local memory plus trainable hyper memory with Mixture-of-Storage), two-stage training on 34B tokens

purpose: Memory foundation models that make persistent, dynamically evolving memory part of the model computation: a constant-size state (about 66x smaller than a full-context KV cache at 128K history) instead of re-reading history (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (Nano tag), MIT (Flash tag)
license.notes: Tags only; no LICENSE file in the Flash repo and the Nano repo was not opened for a file.

architecture.kind: backbone MoE plus native memory blocks (custom code)
architecture.recurrent: memory state updated by a GDN-2 at the end of each turn

pc-12gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
pc-12gb.notes: 22 GB file against 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~3 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-16gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
pc-16gb.notes: 22 GB file against 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~3 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-24gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
pc-24gb.notes: 22 GB file against 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~3 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

pc-32gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
pc-32gb.notes: 22 GB file fits the VRAM budget (29.6 GB) with room for KV

mac-16-24gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
mac-16-24gb.notes: 22 GB file against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
mac-32gb.notes: 22 GB file against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.variant: Nano Q4 by analogy to its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B backbone; no quant published
mac-64gb+.notes: 22 GB file against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

engine_support.notes: Memory blocks are not in any engine we know.

strengths: persistent memory with constant state size is a new axis for long agent sessions
weaknesses: card states that strong textual-memory systems remain ahead overall on its 11 memory benchmarks
soft.maturity: Nano 90k downloads, Flash 58k; paper arXiv 2610.26825 (tag, not read)

tona_fit.reason: Research-grade idea relevant to the long-session coding worker, but it needs custom memory blocks in the engine and the card itself says text memory systems still lead. Watch for a generally supported variant.

open_questions: coding-agent results of the experience-guided framework
